title: In Genesis 6 What Can We Learn From Gods Instructions To Noah About Obedience And Faith
paragraphs: God’s Instructions to Noah: Lessons on Obedience and Faith from Genesis 6

Genesis 6 marks a pivotal moment in redemptive history. Humanity had become corrupt, and God’s judgment was imminent. Yet, amid darkness, Noah found favor in God’s eyes. Through the detailed instructions God gave Noah, we see profound truths about obedience and faith that are still relevant today.
The Context: Corruption and Grace
The world in Noah’s day was filled with violence and evil (Genesis 6:5 ASV). Yet, Noah stood out for his righteousness and blamelessness:
But Noah found favor in the eyes of Jehovah. - Genesis 6:8 ASV
Noah’s relationship with God was characterized by faith and obedience even when everyone around him rebelled.
God’s Specific Instructions
God gave Noah detailed instructions for building the ark and preparing for the flood:
Make thee an ark of gopher wood; rooms shalt thou make in the ark, and shalt pitch it within and without with pitch. - Genesis 6:14 ASV
God outlined the materials, dimensions, and even how the ark should be sealed. Every detail mattered—not for God’s sake, but for Noah’s safety and for the fulfillment of God’s redemptive plan.
Obedience: Complete and Unquestioning
Noah’s response to God’s commands is a model of obedience:
Thus did Noah; according to all that God commanded him, so did he. - Genesis 6:22 ASV
Noah obeyed “all” that God commanded, not just what made sense to him. His obedience was:
Immediate – He acted promptly without delay.
Complete – He followed every detail, not picking and choosing.
Costly – Building the ark required time, resources, and enduring ridicule.
Obedience to God often requires trust even when the world does not understand.
Faith: Trusting God’s Word Without Seeing
Noah had never seen rain or a flood before. Yet, he trusted God’s warning and promise:
By faith Noah, being warned of God concerning things not seen as yet, moved with godly fear, prepared an ark to the saving of his house... - Hebrews 11:7 ASV
Faith believes God’s Word even when circumstances seem impossible. Noah’s faith was not passive; it moved him to action.
What Can We Learn?
God’s Instructions Matter: God’s commands are not arbitrary. Even when we don’t understand the reasons, we are called to obey in faith.
Obedience Is Evidence of Faith: True faith leads to action. As James writes, “faith apart from works is dead” (James 2:26 ASV).
Obedience Can Be Countercultural: Like Noah, we may be called to obey God in ways that others find foolish or unnecessary.
God Honors Faithful Obedience: God saved Noah and his family, using their obedience to preserve life and continue His redemptive plan (Genesis 7:1 ASV).
Pointing to Christ: The ark is a picture of salvation in Christ—those who enter by faith are saved from judgment (John 10:9 ASV).
Conclusion

God’s instructions to Noah challenge us to trust and obey God, even when it is hard or doesn’t make sense. As we follow Him in faith, we become part of His unfolding plan of redemption. Just as Noah was saved by trusting and obeying, so too are we called to respond to Christ in faith and obedience.
